Lina (AM): Quick heads-up — Helios POC is moving to an enterprise commit conversation. They want reserved GPUs with an autoscale fallback and a pricing breakdown that shows cost at committed throughput vs burst. Also asked for answers on the security questionnaire (KMS + audit logs) before legal signs off.

Carlos (SE): Got it. Do we have their traffic shape? qps/rps, avg token length, burst windows? That will drive reserved sizing + preheat plan.

Lina (AM): Summary from the customer: long-tail chat with occasional batch embedding jobs. Requested starting plan: sustained 120 qps with 30s bursts up to ~2k qps for short windows (1–3min). Typical chat requests ~150 tokens in, 90 tokens out on avg. Budget sensitivity around sustained cost — they asked for two numbers: committed monthly + worst-case burst billing.

Carlos (SE): Thanks. For sizing, we need p90/p99 latency SLOs too. Do they need p99 < 300ms?

Lina (AM): They want p95 < 200ms, p99 < 400ms.

Maya (SRE): Recommending approach: reserve a baseline GPU pool to cover the sustained 120 qps (with current model choice), plus a managed burst pool using autoscale + spot where we allow graceful fallbacks. We'll need KV cache warmup and a preheat window before planned marketing spikes. Also recommend cross-AZ spread for eviction tolerance.

Josh (Sales Eng): Can we get a quick back-of-envelope for committed GPUs based on their numbers? Customer expects an "apples-to-apples" committed price vs pay-as-you-go.

Carlos (SE): Back-of-envelope from our perf bench (gpt-variant, quantized): ~1 GPU handles ~40 sustained qps at p95=200ms for avg seq ~240 tokens with batching disabled. With batching and KV caching, you can push that to ~70 qps. For conservative enterprise commit, assume 40 qps per GPU. So for 120 sustained qps => 3 GPUs reserved.

Carlos (SE): For burst capacity to 2k qps, we'd plan an autoscale runway that can spin up additional workers and fall back to a cheaper quantized variant if capacity is constrained. Rough burst sizing: 2k - 120 = 1880 qps additional. If we use the same 40 qps/GPU baseline, that's ~47 GPUs during the peak. Suggest offering burst credits and an SLA that guarantees baseline capacity and best-effort burst.

Maya (SRE): Operational notes: preheat plan to avoid cold KV misses. Recommend a scheduled preheat run 10–15 minutes before expected marketing blasts. Also implement prefix caching for common prompts and warm the KV cache with a synthetic load generator. Example load command we used in staging:

```bash
# run synthetic load to warm caches
./loadgen --target 2000 --concurrency 200 --seq 240 --duration 120
```

Carlos (SE): Also putting a quick traffic profile we got from the customer into the thread to align on numbers:

```text
peak_windows: ["09:30-09:33", "14:00-14:02"]
sustained_qps: 120
burst_peak_qps: 2000
avg_input_tokens: 150
avg_output_tokens: 90
p95_target_ms: 200
p99_target_ms: 400
```

Lina (AM): Security Qs from the questionnaire: KMS customer-managed key required for model inputs + outputs at rest; audit logs retention 1 year; SOC2 + iso27001 certs needed. They also asked about private VPC option.

Maya (SRE): We can support CMK + audit log exports to their SIEM. For Private deployments, we have a VPC path and an on-prem appliance option; that'll affect pricing/contract (platform fee + support tier). I'll attach the checklist for infra items to enable CMK and log exports in the runbook.

Carlos (SE): Pricing shapes to present:
- Committed: 3 reserved GPUs (baseline) + monthly platform fee + 12-month discount => show per-token-equivalent cost and committed monthly invoice.
- Burst: Autoscale up to 47 GPUs (best-effort), bill via burst credits or pay-as-you-go at a higher rate.
- Private deployment: add platform licensing + integration services (one-time).

Josh (Sales Eng): Customer asked if we can cap burst spend. Can we propose a burst credit pool with alerting and hard cap?

Maya (SRE): Yes — we can implement burst credit pools and hard caps at the tenant level; we can also configure automatic fallback to cheaper quantized variants or route to a lower-cost region when cap is hit. That will be part of the ops runbook and the SLA decision table.

Lina (AM): Next steps: Carlos/Maya to draft a one-pager with recommended reserved pool size, burst strategy, and preheat playbook. Josh to prepare pricing slides showing committed vs burst scenarios. Lina to push security questionnaire answers and legal note.

Carlos (SE): I'll drop a short documented runbook + cost calc by EOD.

Maya (SRE): I'll add the KMS + audit log steps and the preheat checklist.

Josh (Sales Eng): I'll sketch the pricing table and include a sample contract language for burst credits.

deploy-bot: Created ticket POC-4521: "Helios enterprise commit — capacity plan + security Qs" assigned to @Carlos @Maya @Josh.

Lina (AM): Great. Can we sync 30m to finalize before we send the answers? :thumbsup:

Carlos (SE): Yes, ping me.

Maya (SRE): Available.

Josh (Sales Eng): On it.

Lina (AM): Meeting booked 30m in #sales. Thanks everyone.
